bugs.error_message: Datadog showed 'set Datadog keys in Settings' but the key inputs were hidden until the source toggle was on
bugs.root_cause: Secret rows were gated on src.enabled, so unavailable sources had no way to set keys before enabling
bugs.fix: Always render secret fields for sources that declare them, independent of the enabled toggle

bugs.error_message: Release workflow run succeeded and packaged archives/SBOMs but created no GitHub Release
bugs.root_cause: The only Release run was a workflow_dispatch on main, so github.ref_type was 'branch'. The args expression selected 'release --snapshot --clean', which builds and packages into dist/ but never publishes; the attestation step was skipped by the same condition. There was no way for a manual run to publish.
bugs.fix: Added an optional workflow_dispatch 'tag' input. A job-level RELEASE_TAG env resolves to github.ref_name on a v* tag push or the dispatch input otherwise; when non-empty the job checks out that tag, runs 'release --clean' with GORELEASER_CURRENT_TAG, and attests provenance. Empty still means a snapshot dry run, now uploading dist as a 'snapshot-dist' artifact.

bugs.error_message: Could not push tag v0.1.0: 'error: RPC failed; HTTP 403' on git-receive-pack for refs/tags/*
bugs.root_cause: A Claude Code remote session's git credentials permit branch pushes (claude/*) but refuse refs/tags/*. Separately, the obvious workaround — creating the release in the GitHub Releases UI — is unsafe with immutable releases enabled: it publishes instantly, so GoReleaser cannot attach assets and the tag name is permanently burnt.
bugs.fix: Added a create_tag checkbox to the Release workflow's workflow_dispatch so the job mints the tag and releases it in one run. Added replace_existing_draft so a mid-upload failure can be retried, and tightened tag validation to a real semver regex since a bad tag would otherwise be pushed before GoReleaser rejects it.

bugs.error_message: release failed after 6m2s - failed to upload triage_0.1.0_linux_i386.rpm.spdx.json: 422 Validation Failed [{Resource:ReleaseAsset Field:name Code:already_exists}]
bugs.root_cause: release.extra_files globbed dist/*.spdx.json, but GoReleaser already uploads every SBOM-typed artifact to the release. All 42 SBOMs were therefore queued twice and the duplicate POST returned 422 already_exists. Snapshot runs never upload, so 4 green snapshot runs could not catch it - it only surfaced on the first real tagged release.
bugs.fix: Removed release.extra_files. checksum.extra_files stays: it only adds the SBOMs as checksums.txt subjects (so provenance covers them) and uploads nothing.

bugs.error_message: Re-running the Release workflow for existing tag v0.1.0 would have reproduced the identical '422 already_exists' SBOM failure even though the fix was already merged to main (caught from the run's head_sha and cancelled before it built)
bugs.root_cause: Publishing an already-existing tag checks out THAT TAG (ref: env.RELEASE_TAG), and GoReleaser reads .goreleaser.yaml from the checked-out tree. Tag v0.1.0 pointed at ff9f062, which predates the PR #13 fix, so the tag's tree still carried the broken release.extra_files glob. A fix merged to main is invisible to a release cut from an older tag. Only the workflow YAML itself comes from the dispatched ref; all repository content comes from the checkout.
bugs.fix: Cut v0.1.1 from main with create_tag=true instead. That path checks out main (which has the fix) and creates the tag there, so GoReleaser reads the corrected config. A tag whose tree contains a broken release config cannot be repaired by fixing main - only by deleting and re-creating the tag, or by moving to a new version number.

bugs.error_message: `go test ./...` listed github.com/polds/rapid-issue-triage/web/node_modules/flatted/golang/pkg/flatted after adding ESLint
bugs.root_cause: eslint -> file-entry-cache -> flat-cache -> flatted, and flatted vendors a Go implementation (flatted.go). Go's `./...` pattern only skips dirs named testdata or starting with . or _, so web/node_modules is walked. It is gitignored, so this only bites after a local `npm install` - CI never installs npm in the Go jobs, which is why CI stayed green.
bugs.fix: Added GO_PKGS (go list ./... filtered through grep -v /node_modules/) and GO_FILES (git ls-files '*.go') to the Makefile and used them in test/test-race/vet/fix-check/fmt-check/vuln. Also added web/node_modules to both exclusions.paths blocks in .golangci.yml.

bugs.error_message: internal/syncer/syncer.go:4:1: package requires newer Go version go1.27 (application built with go1.26) - from `go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@v1.7.0 ./...` and `can't load config: the Go language version (go1.26) used to build golangci-lint is lower than the targeted Go version (1.27.0)` from `make lint`
bugs.root_cause: `go run tool@version` builds the tool in the TOOL's module context, so the toolchain is selected from the tool's go.mod, not this module's. govulncheck v1.7.0 and golangci-lint v2.13.2 both declare go1.26, so both got built with go1.26 and their go/types could not parse a go1.27 module. Local-only: CI's golangci-lint-action downloads a prebuilt binary, and setup-go's environment builds govulncheck with 1.27, so CI on main was green throughout.
bugs.fix: Added GO_TOOLCHAIN = go$(shell go list -m -f '{{.GoVersion}}') to the Makefile (derived from go.mod, so it tracks upgrades) and prefixed the lint and vuln targets with GOTOOLCHAIN=$(GO_TOOLCHAIN). Both now pass locally.

bugs.error_message: ESLint first run: 'X' is defined but never used (NotificationBell.tsx); assertion unnecessary (store.tsx:433); Unexpected iterable of non-Promise values passed to promise aggregator (Macros.tsx:74)
bugs.root_cause: No JS/TS linter had ever run on the frontend, so dead imports, a no-op `as Enrichment` assertion, and a Promise.all fed an array padded with nulls all went unnoticed.
bugs.fix: Removed the unused lucide `X` import, dropped the redundant assertion, and rewrote the Macros reorder to flatMap so only real promises reach Promise.all. Also collapsed SecretField.source from '"settings" | "env" | string' (which TypeScript widens to plain string) to a documented string.

bugs.error_message: CI 'Workflow lint' job failed: .github/workflows/release.yml:78:9: shellcheck reported issue in this script: SC2129:style: Consider using { cmd1; cmd2; } >> file instead of individual redirects [shellcheck]
bugs.root_cause: actionlint shells out to shellcheck for every `run:` block, but only if shellcheck is on PATH - otherwise it silently skips that check and still exits 0. GitHub's ubuntu runners ship shellcheck; this dev container did not. So the local actionlint run looked clean while CI failed on a pre-existing SC2129 in the 'Reproducible timestamps' step (three separate >> "$GITHUB_ENV" redirects). A green local actionlint proves much less than it appears when shellcheck is missing.
bugs.fix: Grouped the three echoes into a single { ... } >> "$GITHUB_ENV" redirect. Installed shellcheck locally and reproduced the failure before fixing. Added a guard to the Makefile actions-lint target: if shellcheck is absent it warns loudly that run: blocks are being skipped, and hard-fails when CI is set, so the blind spot cannot recur silently.

bugs.error_message: fatal: no audit was performed / 'artipacked' audit failed ... couldn't list tags for actions/checkout ... HTTP status client error (401 Unauthorized) for url (https://github.com/actions/checkout.git/git-upload-pack)
bugs.root_cause: zizmor runs online audits by default, which call the GitHub API. Unauthenticated, it does not degrade - it panics and exits non-zero, so no audit runs at all. Every earlier local run had used --no-online-audits, so the first invocation without it (via the new `make actions-lint`) crashed. The CI step as originally written also passed no token and would have hit the same 401 once actionlint stopped failing first.
bugs.fix: Pass --no-online-audits in the Makefile target that both CI and the pre-commit hook call. Deterministic, needs no token, identical locally and in CI; the online audits only check ref freshness, which Dependabot already covers. zizmor stays optional locally but the target hard-fails when CI is set, so a missing binary cannot silently skip the audit.

bugs.error_message: PR #16 stuck: required check 'Web typecheck and build' never reported ('Expected - waiting for status to be reported'), mergeable_state=blocked, while all 14 check runs on the head were green
bugs.root_cause: The Main ruleset (id 21707865, active, strict) requires three status checks by exact name: golangci-lint, 'Web typecheck and build', 'Go fmt, vet, test'. This PR renamed the web job to 'Web lint, test, build' because it now lints and tests too. GitHub matches required checks by name, so the old context can never be satisfied and the PR blocks forever. Not a hung runner - the check was never going to run.
bugs.fix: Owner updates the ruleset to the current job names (and to require the new gates, which were not required at all: Workflow lint, Security, Dependency review, Analyze go, Analyze javascript-typescript, and the three 'Embed UI and compile binary (leg)' matrix names). Documented the trap in README's CI section so a future rename changes the ruleset in the same PR.

bugs.error_message: 422 Validation Failed: "Invalid rule 'tag_name_pattern': " when creating the tag ruleset via POST /repos/polds/rapid-issue-triage/rulesets
bugs.root_cause: tag_name_pattern is a metadata-restriction rule. That family is plan/ownership gated and is not available on this user-owned repository, so the API rejects the rule outright. The recommended ruleset JSON included it without checking availability first - the REST schema documents the rule's shape but not which repos may use it.
bugs.fix: Dropped the rule. The 'Release Tags' ruleset ships deletion + non_fast_forward + update, which are the rules that actually protect published Go module versions. Semver enforcement stays in release.yml's regex guard; the release workflow's v*.*.* trigger glob means a non-semver tag cannot start a release anyway.

bugs.error_message: OpenWolf protocol commands unavailable in Claude Code sessions: `openwolf scan` / `find` / `designqc` not found, so .wolf/anatomy.md could only be maintained by hand and drifted (last scan tracked 90 files while the tree had 121).
bugs.root_cause: The .wolf/hooks/*.js are committed and run under node, so the hooks fired normally and nothing looked broken - but the `openwolf` CLI they document is a global npm install, and Claude Code on the web uses ephemeral containers where a global install does not survive into the next session. Nothing reinstalled it, so every CLI-dependent step of .wolf/OPENWOLF.md silently had no way to run.
bugs.fix: Added .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (adopted from a sibling repo) and registered it first in .claude/settings.json's SessionStart, so the CLI is reinstalled at the start of every remote session before .wolf/hooks/session-start.js runs. Guarded to CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true, idempotent, fail-soft. Its `openwolf init` step is correctly skipped here because .wolf/ is tracked. Verified by running it: openwolf 2.5.0 installed, init skipped, `openwolf scan` then reindexed 121 files.

bugs.error_message: Confetti particles jumped mid-burst: all 60 pieces re-randomized on every re-render
bugs.root_cause: The piece array was built inline in the render body with Math.random(), so every parent re-render produced a brand-new set of positions and tones while the burst animation was still running. react-hooks/purity flagged it once the rule was enabled.
bugs.fix: Extracted rollPieces() and roll the array once per burst (keyed state), so a re-render reuses the same pieces.

bugs.error_message: react-hooks/set-state-in-effect still reported after prefixing the call with `void`
bugs.root_cause: `void f()` only discards the promise, which satisfies no-floating-promises. set-state-in-effect tracks the setter reached from the effect body, so the report is unchanged.
bugs.fix: Wrapped the work in an effect-owned async IIFE: `void (async () => { ... })()`.

bugs.error_message: Reported '7 required checks failing' on PR #26 when nothing was failing
bugs.root_cause: The check-status script deduplicated check runs by name and kept whichever the API returned first. After a re-run several runs share a name; the stale cancelled ones won. The real state was 8 cancelled + 7 in progress.
bugs.fix: Keep the latest run per name by started_at before evaluating conclusions.

bugs.error_message: sonarjs/super-linear-regex: Markdown.tsx inline tokenizer went quadratic - 160KB of `"[a](".repeat(n)` took ~2.5s to split (4x input -> 17x time)
bugs.root_cause: The link alternative `\[[^\]]+\]\([^)]+\)` bounded the target with `[^)]+`, which does not exclude the `(` that opens it. With no `)` ahead, every `[` position rescanned to end-of-string. Issue bodies are untrusted Linear-authored text, so this was reachable ReDoS.
bugs.fix: Bounded both negated classes by their own opening delimiter: `\[[^\][\n]+\]\([^()\s]+\)`, and matched the same shape in the re-parse regex below it. 2529ms -> 1ms at 160KB. Cost: a link target containing a space or a paren now renders as text.

bugs.error_message: `make quality` printed 'no unreachable functions' and exited 0 while deadcode had actually failed with 'packages contain errors / exit status 1'
bugs.root_cause: The target captured the tool's stdout into `$out` and only tested whether it was non-empty. deadcode writes its errors to stderr and exits non-zero, so a build failure produced an empty $out and read as a clean run - exactly the silent no-op the repo's CI conventions forbid.
bugs.fix: Trap the assignment's exit status: `out="$(...)" || { echo ...; exit 1; }` before the emptiness test. Verified with `sh -c 'out="$(false)" || ...'`.

bugs.error_message: deadcode reported store.MarkTriaged and QueueFilter.Empty as unreachable; deleting them broke `go fix -diff` and the store tests
bugs.root_cause: `deadcode -test ./cmd/triage` only treats the *listed* packages' tests as entry points. Both functions are exercised by internal/store's own tests, which were therefore invisible. A grep that should have caught it was run from web/ after the shell cwd had changed, and returned nothing.
bugs.fix: Run `deadcode -test $(GO_PKGS)` over every package so each one's tests count as entry points; both functions were restored. Check the shell's cwd before trusting an empty grep.

bugs.error_message: The new License scan gate passed while eslint-plugin-sonarjs@4.2.0 (LGPL-3.0-only) sat in the tree, even though WEB_LICENSE_DENY listed LGPL-3.0. Caught by socket-security[bot] on PR #41, not by the gate.
bugs.root_cause: The deny check compared raw SPDX strings. SPDX has two spellings for every GPL-family license -- the modern `LGPL-3.0-only`/`GPL-2.0-or-later` and the deprecated bare `LGPL-3.0` -- so a policy written in one spelling silently misses the other. The gate failed open on exactly the class it existed to catch.
bugs.fix: Normalise both sides before comparing: strip a trailing `-only`/`-or-later`/`+` and upper-case, so one policy entry matches every spelling. Added a `selftest()` that asserts the matcher against both spellings plus a dual-licensed expression on every run, and verified it fails when the normaliser is removed. Separately, the dev tier was narrowed (LGPL/MPL/EPL dropped) after a policy decision: dev tooling is executed, never conveyed.

bugs.error_message: Bash tool call exited 144 with no output at all when the command began with `pkill -f rapid-issue-triage/triage`
bugs.root_cause: pkill -f matches against full command lines, and the shell running the Bash tool call has the pattern in its own argv, so pkill killed its own caller before the rest of the command ran.
bugs.fix: Never use `pkill -f` with a pattern that appears in the invoking command. driver.mjs stop kills by recorded pidfile and by scanning /proc/*/exe for the repo's ./triage binary instead.

bugs.error_message: POST /api/issues/{id}/macro/1 returned 404 {"error":"not found"} right after seeding three macros
bugs.root_cause: macros.id is AUTOINCREMENT, so `DELETE FROM macros` leaves sqlite_sequence untouched and each re-seed hands out ids continuing from the previous high-water mark (10, 11, 12) rather than 1, 2, 3.
bugs.fix: The fixture now runs DELETE FROM sqlite_sequence WHERE name IN ('macros','activity') after wiping, so macro ids are stable at 1..3 across re-seeds.

bugs.error_message: playwright waitForSelector timed out: "locator resolved to 6 elements" while waiting for text=/skip|snooze/i to check the help overlay
bugs.root_cause: The words Skip and Snooze are also the card's own action buttons, so a loose text= selector matched visible page chrome and never proved the dialog opened.
bugs.fix: Anchor on the dialog heading instead: h2:text-is("Keyboard shortcuts"). Same class of fix for the other routes (h1:text-is("Reports") etc).

bugs.error_message: Driver navigated to #/report and screenshotted the triage deck, with the assertion still passing
bugs.root_cause: web/src/App.tsx pageFromHash() only recognises macros|reports|settings and silently falls back to 'triage' for anything else, so a typo'd route renders the wrong page instead of erroring.
bugs.fix: Use the exact route name 'reports', and assert on a heading unique to the target page so a silent fallback fails loudly.

bugs.error_message: Error: unable to open database file (ERR_SQLITE_ERROR errcode 14) when seeding after `rm -rf .run-sandbox`
bugs.root_cause: The driver adopted a server that was already listening on 7333, so it skipped writeConfig() and never recreated the sandbox dir; node:sqlite then could not create the db file. The Go store owns the DDL, so seeding a path the server never opened has no schema either way.
bugs.fix: cmdSmoke now calls writeConfig() unconditionally, and seed() fails with an explicit 'start the server once first' message when the db file is absent.

bugs.error_message: git status showed web/dist/index.html modified and a renamed assets/index-*.js after `make build` on an unmodified tree
bugs.root_cause: The `ui` target runs `npm install --no-fund --no-audit` rather than `npm ci`, so transitive dependency resolution can diverge from the lockfile and Vite emits a bundle with a different content hash. `make web-ci` does not hit this: its `web-deps` step uses `npm ci`.
bugs.fix: Not a code change. Check `git status -- web/dist` after `make build`: if the UI changed, stage the rebuild (what `make web-dist-check` wants); if nothing changed, `git checkout -- web/dist/` and delete the stray asset. Did not reproduce after main's lockfile update in 64cbf6c, so it is lockfile-state dependent rather than a standing property of the target.

bugs.error_message: Action failed: linear: labelIds not exclusive child labels — running a macro that adds a label from Linear's "Area" group onto an issue that already carries a sibling of that group
bugs.root_cause: Linear label groups are mutually exclusive (only one child per group per issue), but nothing indexed the parent edge: internal/linear did not request IssueLabel.parent, the labels table had no parent_id, and resolveOps built labelIds with no exclusivity check. The clash only surfaced as Linear's own opaque rejection, after the card had already swiped away.
bugs.fix: Sync parent { id } into labels.parent_id (additive migration) and add store.LabelGroupsFor. resolveOps now ends in resolveLabelGroups, which returns a structured *labelGroupError naming the group and both sides; handlers answer 409 {code, conflicts, resolvable} via writeActionErr. opOptions.replaceGroupLabels drops the pre-existing sibling once the user confirms. The UI pre-flights the same rule in web/src/lib/labelgroups.ts and raises LabelGroupPrompt (Replace / Cancel) before the request, and exclusiveLabelHint rewrites Linear's wording for a group created since the last sync.

bugs.error_message: SAST job failed on PR #46: go.lang.security.audit.database.string-formatted-query at internal/store/metadata.go — 1 finding, 1 blocking
bugs.root_cause: LabelGroupsFor built its dynamic IN clause as `q := "SELECT ... IN (?" + strings.Repeat(", ?", n-1) + ")"` and passed q to db.Query in the same function. Semgrep's rule matches a query variable initialized from a string literal concatenated with an expression and then handed to Query — the args were always bound, so it is a false positive on injection, but a real style divergence: issues.go:85 does the same dynamic IN clause and is NOT flagged because it appends with `+=` to an existing query variable.
bugs.fix: Split the literal from the placeholder list (`q := ...IN (` then `q += placeholders(len(ids)) + ")"`), matching issues.go, and reuse the `placeholders` helper already in queuefilter.go instead of a second open-coded strings.Repeat. Reproduced and verified with the pinned semgrep 1.175.0: 1 blocking finding before, 0 after.

bugs.error_message: Filtering the Labels picker showed two stacked picker panels — the typed/filtered list on top and the full unfiltered list behind it, each with its own "Enter toggles · Esc closes" footer
bugs.root_cause: TriagePage mounts QuickEditRow twice for the responsive layout — once under the card (xl:hidden) and once in the wide rail (hidden xl:flex) — and both shared the same `picker` state. QuickEditRow rendered the <Picker> itself, and Picker uses createPortal(..., document.body), which escapes the wrapper doing the responsive hiding. So both instances portalled a panel to body regardless of viewport width, each with independent query/cursor state; the last-mounted one took focus, leaving the other rendered unfiltered behind it.
bugs.fix: Split the component: QuickEditRow now renders only the buttons (safe to duplicate — they are in-flow and CSS-hidden), and a new QuickEditPickers holds the Picker + DuplicateOfPicker and is rendered exactly once by TriagePage off the same shared `open` state. Verified in the running app: 2 panels before, 1 after. Invariant recorded in web/src/components/triage/CLAUDE.md.

bugs.error_message: Action failed: not found — occasional error on Skip or Snooze
bugs.root_cause: The deck the browser holds is a snapshot; the background syncer's PruneStale(gen) DELETEs every issue whose sync_gen fell behind, i.e. any issue that left the index filter (triaged, closed or reassigned in Linear since the batch was fetched). Skip and snooze then POST against a row that is gone: handleSkip/handleSnooze call store.GetIssue, errRow turns sql.ErrNoRows into the bare error "not found", and the handler answered writeErr(w, 404, err). The UI's swipeAway rolled the card back and toasted "Action failed: <message>", stranding the user on a card no keystroke could clear. Occasional because it needs a sync tick to land between the queue fetch and the keypress.
bugs.fix: store.ErrNotFound is now an exported sentinel (same message, errors.Is-able). New server helper writeIssueErr answers a pruned row with 404 {code:"issue_gone"} plus an explanation, and anything that is not ErrNotFound with a 500 (it used to 404 those too); all six GetIssue(r.PathValue("id")) sites use it. The UI adds a "gone" CardStatus and retireGoneCard: on code issue_gone skip/snooze mark the card gone ("LEFT THE INDEX" badge, actions disabled), advance the deck, and show a plain informational toast instead of an error. Verified live via the driver by DELETEing the visible card's row from sqlite behind the deck's back.

bugs.error_message: `./triage -version` on a locally built binary printed `triage v0.0.0-20260831170347-5fc31f49c73e+dirty`, and the update check treated that build as a release (so any real tag looked like an available upgrade)
bugs.root_cause: Resolve fell back to debug.ReadBuildInfo().Main.Version when -ldflags stamped nothing. For a `go build` inside a checkout the toolchain synthesizes a pseudo-version (vX.Y.Z-<14-digit timestamp>-<12 hex>), which parses as a perfectly valid v0.0.0 prerelease — so Dev was false and IsNewer said yes to every published tag.
bugs.fix: Added a pseudoVersion regexp (`[-.]<14 digits>-<12 hex>` with optional build metadata) and reject a Main.Version matching it, keeping "dev" and taking only vcs.revision/vcs.time. A dev build is now never offered an update. Note the second form: `v1.2.4-0.<timestamp>-<hash>` separates with a dot, not a dash — anchoring on `-` alone missed it.

bugs.error_message: Reports page: Outcome breakdown legend misaligned - the '37 · 26%' value wrapped onto two lines and counts/percents did not line up down the list
bugs.root_cause: The donut legend rendered count and share as one ml-auto string ('{value} · {pct}%'), so in the narrow lg:grid-cols-[1.6fr_1fr] card the pair wrapped mid-string and every row's numbers started at a different x.
bugs.fix: Split the pair into two fixed-min-width, right-aligned tabular-nums columns (min-w-7 count, min-w-8 percent), gave the label min-w-0 flex-1 truncate and the dot shrink-0, and shrank the donut from size-44/gap-5 to size-40/gap-4 to free legend width.
